question.text: Iran says the US talks up negotiations to lower oil prices; the US says Iran's demands are unreasonable. Pick one side and write its strongest honest case. What does it need the other side to believe, and what would change its mind?

topics.heading: Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi go to a second day, focused on prisoners
topics.summary: US-brokered talks between Russian and Ukrainian delegations continued in Abu Dhabi for a second day, the first such meeting in nine months.[^1] Zelenskyy called day one "constructive and quite substantive", with prisoner releases the main focus; neither side has dropped its core demands.[^1][^2]

lead.title: Russia and Ukraine hold a second day of US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi

alsoReported.title: 2nd day of trilateral peace talks begins between Ukraine, Russia, US in Abu Dhabi

article: Delegations from Russia and Ukraine met for a second straight day on Wednesday in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner mediating. It is the first round between the two sides since February in Geneva. On Tuesday they talked for about four hours.[^1]

Ukraine's team is led by Rustem Umerov, the head of its foreign intelligence service; Russia's is led by Vladimir Medinsky, an aide to President Putin who also negotiated in 2022 and 2025.[^2] Zelenskyy said the first day was "constructive and quite substantive" and that "the release of prisoners is a priority". Talks also covered returning civilians and children, and how security guarantees for Ukraine could work over the long term.[^1][^2] US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the meeting "very productive" but said a breakthrough would take time.[^1]

Europe is in the room next door, not at the table. Moscow does not want European countries in the direct talks, so national security advisers from France, Germany, the UK and Italy, plus EU and NATO officials, met the Ukrainian and US teams separately.[^2][^1]

The war continued around the talks. Russia's Defence Ministry said it downed 627 Ukrainian drones overnight, 150 of them over the St. Petersburg region, and a regional governor said drones started a fire at Ust-Luga, one of Russia's main oil export ports. Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia and Kharkiv wounded seven civilians, AP reports.[^1]

My read: humanitarian steps such as a prisoner exchange are the most realistic result this week. The hard questions, the land Russia still demands and who would guarantee any deal, remain far apart. Watch whether the envoys travel to Moscow and Kyiv, and whether the topic returns at next week's APEC summit in China.

topics.heading: Iran denies any talks with the US and says Hormuz stays shut until its demands are met
topics.summary: Iran's security chief called reports of US-Iran negotiations "a pure lie" and said the Strait of Hormuz stays closed until Washington meets seven conditions.[^3] Qatar, the main go-between, said a day earlier it had seen "progress".[^4]

lead.title: Iran denies talks with US, says Hormuz will stay shut until demands are met

alsoReported.title: Qatar sees 'progress' in US-Iran talks after White House meeting

article: The war that began in February is now in its ninth month, and the two sides are describing the same moment very differently. On Monday, after meeting Qatar's prime minister at the White House, President Trump said he saw "positive momentum" and that new attacks on Iran were unnecessary for now, while keeping the US naval blockade of Iranian ports in place.[^3][^4]

On Tuesday, Qatar's foreign ministry said it had seen "progress", though its spokesperson added that "we cannot say how close or how far away an agreement is".[^4] Then on Wednesday, Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran's top security council, told Lebanon's Al Mayadeen TV that reports of negotiations or a meeting in Qatar were "a pure lie" meant to calm oil prices. He said the US's first reply to Iran's seven conditions was "insufficient and deceptive".[^3]

Iran has not published the full list. Officials say it includes lifting sanctions and the blockade and ending fighting on all fronts, especially Israel's strikes on Lebanon. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says the strait could reopen within two days if the demands are met.[^3] In Paris, Secretary of State Rubio said the US is "open to diplomacy" and that its economic pressure is strong enough that "there is no need for major combat operations".[^3]

The strait matters because a large share of the world's oil and liquefied gas normally passes through it. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said three tankers caught fire after hitting mines on an "unauthorised route" on Tuesday, and maritime monitors count at least 37 attacks on ships near Hormuz so far in November, the most of any month in the war.[^3]

My read: both sides gain from appearing reasonable to Gulf states and to oil markets, which is why the public messages diverge. The test is concrete: a confirmed meeting, an eased blockade, or ships moving safely.
topics.differences: The US and Qatar describe progress and momentum toward talks.[^4] Iran's security chief says there are no talks at all and calls the reports a US ploy to lower oil prices.[^3]

topics.heading: US and China plan a dialogue on 'superintelligence' at next week's Xi meeting
topics.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said a meeting with Xi Jinping next week will launch a US-China dialogue on very advanced AI, including a direct channel to warn each other of serious incidents.[^5]

lead.title: US and China should stay clear-eyed on AI cooperation and competition, Bessent says

article: Speaking in New York on Tuesday to the National Committee on US-China Relations, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC summit on Nov 18-19. That meeting, he said, will launch a two-way dialogue on "superintelligence", meaning AI systems that could outperform people at most tasks, with the stated aim to "prevent a misunderstanding between our two systems".[^5]

According to Reuters, the two governments will exchange best practices for testing advanced AI models before release and have agreed on a direct channel to alert each other to serious AI incidents.[^5] Channels like this already exist for military crises; the idea is to have a phone line ready before something goes wrong, not after.

Bessent was careful not to sound warm. He said both countries "should harbor no illusions" about their differences and that US policy is to "de-risk, not to decouple", meaning reduce dependence on China without cutting ties. He also described planned boards to agree mutual tariff cuts on about $30 billion of non-sensitive goods each way.[^5]

The backdrop is tense. Nvidia, the leading AI chip maker, is investigating whether its chief executive was targeted by Chinese intelligence; China's foreign ministry calls the accusations "groundless".[^5] Bessent did not mention the case.

My read: an incident channel is a modest step, and the details are so far known from one Reuters report. Still, it would be the first formal US-China arrangement aimed at the most powerful AI systems. Watch what the two sides actually sign in Shenzhen.

topics.heading: Indonesia's vice president offers to resign after a court rules against his documents
topics.summary: Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka, son of former president Joko Widodo, offered to resign in a meeting with President Prabowo Subianto after a court found his school documents did not meet election rules.[^6][^7]

lead.title: Indonesia's vice president offers resignation as questions mount over his eligibility

alsoReported.title: Breaking News: Gibran Offers to Resign as Indonesia's Vice President Amid Diploma Dispute

article: Indonesia is the world's fourth most populous country and Southeast Asia's largest economy. On Tuesday its vice president, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, 39, offered to resign during a meeting of more than two hours with President Prabowo Subianto, according to State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi.[^6][^7]

The dispute is about paperwork. Gibran finished his secondary schooling abroad, and last month Indonesia's Supreme Court found that the education documents he submitted for the 2024 election did not meet the requirements.[^6] Some lawmakers then called for his impeachment. Gibran said he did not want the situation "to become a prolonged political controversy" but did not speak about the offer directly.[^6]

It is not clear what happens next. Prasetyo said it was "not true" that Prabowo had rejected the offer, but no written resignation was announced and no constitutional process has begun.[^7] Prabowo advised Gibran to keep defending his documents in court, and Gibran asked for a chance to do that at the State Administrative Court.[^6][^7]

The case also reflects a wider split. Gibran is the son of Joko Widodo, the popular former president whose backing helped Prabowo win in 2024. AP reports a widening rift between Prabowo and Widodo, who separately denies allegations that he used a fake university diploma.[^6]
My read: the immediate question is legal, but the bigger one is political, about who holds power in Prabowo's coalition. Watch the court case and whether parliament begins any formal process.

topics.heading: South Africa's ANC falls to about 31% in local elections, its worst since apartheid
topics.summary: Final results show the ANC, Nelson Mandela's party, at 30.76% nationally, down from 45.59% in 2021; the Democratic Alliance leads in five of the eight big metro areas.[^8][^9]

alsoReported.title: African National Congress Suffers Its Worst Election Result Since South Africa Ended Apartheid

article: South Africa's electoral commission has finished counting the 2026 local government elections. The African National Congress, which has led the country since the end of apartheid in 1994, won 30.76% of the national vote, down almost 15 points from 45.59% in 2021.[^8] It remains the largest party, but this is its worst result since apartheid ended.[^9]

The Democratic Alliance (DA), the main rival, rose to 24.64%. Next came the MK party of former president Jacob Zuma at 9.77%, the Economic Freedom Fighters at 6.22% and ActionSA at 5.67%.[^8] The DA says it won more than a million votes from Black South Africans for the first time, which matters because it has long been seen as a party of mostly white and mixed-race voters.[^9]

The cities show the shift most clearly. The DA leads in five of eight metros, including Johannesburg (34.79% to the ANC's 20.25%) and Cape Town (56.42%). In eThekwini, which includes Durban, MK took 38.29%. The ANC leads only in Buffalo City and, narrowly, Mangaung.[^8]

Local councils run water, electricity distribution, roads and rubbish collection, so many results now depend on coalitions. ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula said "the people of South Africa have spoken" and the party would respond "with introspection"; the DA says coalition talks will be handled nationally.[^8] The two parties already govern together nationally after the ANC lost its majority in 2024.
My read: the result shows a long decline continuing rather than a sudden break. The next test is whether city coalitions can deliver basic services more reliably than before.

topics.heading: Brazil presents a road map away from fossil fuels at COP31
topics.summary: On COP31's energy day in Antalya, Brazil presented a voluntary road map for moving away from coal, oil and gas, and the UN chief urged countries to set timelines.[^10][^11]

lead.title: Brazil presents road map away from fossil fuels and toward renewable energies at UN climate talks

alsoReported.title: COP31: Energy transition takes centre stage as countries map path beyond fossil fuels

article: On Tuesday, the second day of the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, Brazil presented a road map for a "transition away from fossil fuels".[^10] Brazil hosted last year's summit, COP30, where countries could not agree on such a plan, so it wrote one itself. The document is voluntary and is not a new binding agreement.[^11]

It lists "levers" countries can pull, such as halting new fossil fuel power plants and cutting fossil fuel subsidies.[^10] Ana Toni, who leads Brazil's COP30 team, said the aim is to be "very pragmatic" and told countries to "start now from wherever you are".[^10][^11] Brazil is itself a major oil exporter, a tension Toni declined to discuss directly.[^10]

UN Secretary-General António Guterres linked the plan to this year's oil shock. He said the European Union alone has paid more than €100 billion in extra fossil fuel import costs since the Middle East escalation began, and that fuel prices rose in 130 countries. "Disruption anywhere drives up prices everywhere," he said, asking countries for national plans with timelines by 2028.[^11]

Host Turkey is promoting a pledge to raise electricity's share of world energy use to 35% by 2035, from about 23% today, according to AP.[^10] A UN expert noted that about 2,500 gigawatts of projects worldwide are waiting to be connected to power grids.[^11] The US government is absent for a second year; former envoy John Kerry said "we don't need more promises, we need plans".[^10]

My read: a voluntary road map cannot force anyone to act, but the Iran war has made the economic case for cutting oil dependence easier to argue. The final COP31 text, due next week, will show how many countries sign up to anything concrete.
